03 / THE SHORT GUIDE

Less jargon. More clarity.

Three things worth knowing before you head out.

01

PM2.5 for right now

These tiny particles can get deep into your lungs. The 1-hour reading tells you how much was in the air over the past hour. It can change quickly, so check again before heading out.

02

PSI for the bigger picture

Singapore’s 24-hour PSI combines several pollutants over a longer period. It is useful for planning, but it may respond more slowly to a sudden change outside your window.

03

There isn’t one global AQI

Different countries calculate “AQI” differently. We show NEA’s original Singapore readings and official bands, so you can see exactly what each number means here.

THE MASK, EXPLAINED

04 / A QUICK MASK CHECK

Do I need a mask?

For a short commute or while indoors, MOH says an N95 is generally unnecessary. If you must spend extended time outdoors when readings are high, a well-fitting respirator can reduce exposure.

  • ✓Look for N95 or equivalent. KN95, FFP2 and KF94 are comparable categories, according to MOH.
  • ✓Fit matters. It needs a close seal around your nose and mouth. A loose surgical mask is not the same protection against fine particles.
  • ✓Put health first. If breathing is difficult, take a break. People with severe heart or lung conditions, older adults and pregnant people should check with a doctor before using one.
Read MOH’s full mask advice ↗

05 / SMALL, USEFUL MOVES

A little less exposure.

Move the workout in

Swap the run for an indoor session when the air is elevated or high.

Make indoors more comfortable

During sustained haze, close windows and use air filtration if available.

Check again before leaving

Haze can shift within hours. A fresh reading is more useful than a screenshot from earlier.

THE FINE PRINT, MADE CLEAR

Where the numbers
come from.

No secret formulas and no hidden sensors. Readings come directly from Singapore’s NEA through data.gov.sg’s public real-time API. Advice and bands follow NEA and MOH guidance.
